meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بزعج, بيزعج).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
Sorry if we disturbed you at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باكل, بياكل).

examples.trans: The brothers are eating lemon cake in the courtyard.
We ate a hot breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتغل, بيشتغل).

examples.trans: Look, the flame came on blue!
He works on heritage buildings in Amman.

meanings.note: In Amman, وسط البلد or simply البلد refers to downtown Amman.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
Town is quiet on Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بنايات.

examples.trans: The stone building is eighty years old.
The building owner sent a letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: As a noun after على (على بعد عشر أمتار 'at a distance of ten metres'); distinct from preposition بعد ('after').

examples.trans: The shop is five minutes away.
The stop is a hundred metres away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تراثية, plural: تراثيين).

examples.trans: He works on restoring heritage buildings in Amman.

examples.text: هاد بيت تراثي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: This is a historic house eighty years old.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Quick thinking solved the problem.
That is smart, logical thinking.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eighty'.

examples.text: خشب بلوط أصلي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: Solid oak wood eighty years old.
This house has lived through eighty winters!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحب, بيحب).

examples.trans: I liked working here so much more!
Would you like coffee or black tea?

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

حِفِظ.gloss: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve

meanings.en: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحفظ, بيحفظ).

examples.trans: Old stone holds the warmth until morning.

examples.text: شكرا لأنك حفظت الشنتة طول الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Thank you for keeping the bag safe all week.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fifteen' before a counted noun (خمستعشر سنة 'fifteen years').

examples.trans: I have not seen it in fifteen years!
The landing is after fifteen steps.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافعة, plural: دافعين).

examples.text: ما بدنا نزعج ضيف دافع حق غرفته.
examples.trans: We do not want to bother a paying guest.
All the guests have paid the bill in advance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدفن, بيدفن).

examples.text: لا تدفنا قبل ما نقرأ الورقة كلها!
examples.trans: Do not bury us before we read the whole sheet!
He buried the key in a small box.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ذكية, plural: أذكياء).

examples.trans: Smart, quick thinking, Nour!
A clever idea solved the problem right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: راجعة, plural: راجعين).

examples.trans: I am running right back across the bridge now!
Salma is coming back from the table.

راح.gloss: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)

meanings.en: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بروح, بيروح).

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: روس.

examples.trans: My glasses were on my head!

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من السقف الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low ceiling.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتب, بيرتب).

examples.trans: Life arranges sweeter melodies than we do.
I straighten my ties and keys every day.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسايل.

examples.trans: An official letter arrived at noon.
We read the letter line by line.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سخانات.

examples.trans: We started the boiler before breakfast.
The boiler room is down in the basement.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شتويات.

examples.trans: This house has lived through eighty winters.
Last winter was cold and long.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

شوي.gloss: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)

meanings.en: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)
meanings.note: Means 'a bit / a moment' (استنوا شوي 'wait a moment'); doubled شوي شوي means 'slowly, gently'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صحاب.

examples.trans: Who is the owner of the blue suitcase?
We became friends from the first day.

meanings.note: Everyday word confirming something is right ('right! / true!').

examples.text: صح! في صفحة تانية ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: Right! There is a second page behind the letter.
What you say is completely true.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صمامات.

examples.trans: We fitted a new brass valve on the boiler.
Make sure the valve is tightly shut.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعيش, بيعيش).

examples.trans: This house has lived through eighty winters!
They lived in our quarter for many years.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فقرات.

examples.trans: We read all the paragraphs in the contract.
The second paragraph clarifies the law.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاعدة, plural: قاعدين).

examples.trans: Who is sitting in our courtyard under the tree?
We are sitting having tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قوانين.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects historic houses.
Rami knows building regulations well.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قانونية, plural: قانونيين).

examples.trans: Legal clauses are hard to read.
The lease contract is legal and protected.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كرافات.

examples.trans: He arranged the blue ties in the wardrobe.
A drop of juice landed on my tie!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كيكات.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمع, بيلمع).

examples.trans: Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

examples.text: خمستعشر سنة وأنا بلمع مفاتيح النحاس!
examples.trans: Fifteen years I have been polishing the brass keys!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'yesterday' (مبارح بالليل 'last night').

examples.trans: Look what arrived last night!
I booked the room by phone yesterday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مباني.

examples.text: المباني القديمة بعمان مبنية من حجر.
examples.trans: Old buildings in Amman are built of stone.
He works in restoring heritage buildings.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أمتار.

examples.trans: The table is ten metres away.
The courtyard is eight metres wide.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مستحيلة, plural: —).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
It is impossible for us to forget this week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مشبوكة, plural: مشبوكين).

examples.text: في صفحة تانية مشبوكة ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: There is a second page clipped behind the letter.
The lamp is plugged in.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مشاكل.

examples.trans: There is no problem at all with your booking.
Every problem has a simple solution.

meanings.note: Plural-form noun that is THE everyday Jordanian/Levantine word for money.

examples.trans: Take cash from the box for the shop.
We saved money for annual maintenance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معمارية, plural: معماريين).

examples.trans: I am an architectural acoustics engineer.

examples.text: حجر عمان إله طابع معماري جميل.
examples.trans: Amman stone has a beautiful architectural character.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مكسورة, plural: مكسورين).

examples.trans: Put the broken valve in your coat pocket.
We fixed the broken chair leg.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مهندسين.

examples.trans: His brother is a skilled architect in Amman.
The engineer inspected the walls of the old building.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'who?' (لمين 'whose? / for whom?').

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, نحاس covers both yellow brass and red copper, often placed directly after a noun (مفاتيح نحاس brass keys).

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أوجاع.

examples.trans: Tiny numbers give me a headache!

examples.text: راح وجع الراس بعد فنجان القهوة.
examples.trans: The headache went away after a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of وراء ('behind, past').

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.
